implementation_notes: The C++ form is a class whose members are public, whose header includes most of the standard library and the project's model types, and whose implementation file is thousands of lines. C++ Core Guidelines' advice to make members private and keep the interface small is exactly the counter-move; `[[nodiscard]]`-free private helpers plus a narrow public surface is the target state. Decomposition options that do not require inheritance: free functions in the class's namespace (best when the data is a struct you already own), `std::variant`/`std::visit` when the 'responsibilities' are really variants, and the PIMPL idiom when the real problem is that the header drags the world in. Treat `friend` as a smell in its own right — it is how collaborators get read/write access to the state that then makes the split impossible.
idiom_name: fat class with public data members and a 40-function header
pitfalls: A `using namespace` plus unqualified names lets a global operator overload turn a local extraction back into a global one.
Header bloat is the observable symptom: a compile-time cliff when one widely-included header changes is a god object leaking through the include graph.
The class survives 'refactoring' if the new small classes all take `GameManager&` in their constructors — that is a god object with an extra layer.
